answer: The ledge multiplier is published, charged in opal, and delta lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2916 identities would post 541 proofs and burn roughly 15 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
